title: SUPG, residual stabilization and variational multiscale methods

items.title: One-dimensional stationary convection–diffusion model and uniform P1 space
items.statement:
Fix an integer $N\ge1$, put $h=1/N$, and let $x_j=jh$ for $j=0,\ldots,N$. The cells are $K_j=[x_{j-1},x_j]$. For $g_0,g_1\in\mathbb R$, let $S_h(g_0,g_1)$ be the finite-dimensional space of continuous functions on $[0,1]$ that are affine on each cell and have endpoint values $g_0,g_1$. Write $V_h=S_h(0,0)$ for the homogeneous test and trial space. “P1” means polynomial degree at most one on each interval.

Let $\epsilon>0$, $b\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, and $f\in C([0,1])$. The stationary boundary-value problem is to find $u\in C^2([0,1])$ such that $-\epsilon u''+b u'=f$ on $(0,1)$, with prescribed endpoint values $u(0)=g_0$ and $u(1)=g_1$. Its dimensionless cell Péclet number is $\mathrm{Pe}=|b|h/(2\epsilon)>0$. The stability theorem on this page uses the homogeneous branch $g_0=g_1=0$; the general endpoint notation also permits the boundary-layer example.

items.title: Stationary multidimensional convection–diffusion–reaction P1 model
items.statement:
Fix $d\ge2$ and a bounded connected polyhedral open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$. For each mesh parameter $h$, let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite matching shape-regular affine simplicial mesh in the sense of [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], and put $h=\max_{K\in\mathcal T_h}h_K$. Let $V_h$ be the space of continuous functions on $\overline\Omega$ that are affine on every cell and vanish on $\partial\Omega$.

Let $\epsilon>0$, $b\in C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$, $c\in C(\overline\Omega)$, and $f\in C(\overline\Omega)$. Define $B:=\|b\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}$ and $C:=\|c\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}$. Assume a fixed $\omega>0$ satisfies $c-\frac12\nabla\cdot b\ge\omega$ on $\Omega$. The boundary condition for this branch is $u=0$ on the whole boundary, including the inflow part $\{x\in\partial\Omega:b(x)\cdot n(x)<0\}$. A classical exact solution is a function $u\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$ satisfying $-\epsilon\Delta u+b\cdot\nabla u+cu=f$ in $\Omega$ and this boundary condition.

items.title: Residual PSPG and grad-div terms for equal-order flow spaces
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ have a finite cell partition $\mathcal T$. Let $V_h$ be a finite-dimensional vector space of continuous vector-valued functions, each cellwise polynomial, and let $Q_h$ be a finite-dimensional scalar space of continuous cellwise polynomials with zero mean. Boundary conditions are stated with each application; the Stokes theorem below uses zero velocity boundary values, and the periodic example below uses periodic identification. The pair is **equal order** when velocity components and pressure use the same polynomial degree on each cell. On a cell $K$, derivatives in residuals are classical derivatives restricted to the cell interior. For well-defined cell integrals, take $\sigma\in L^\infty(\Omega)$, $ eta\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$, $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$, and parameters $	au_K\ge0$, $\gamma\ge0$.

For viscosity $
u>0$, reaction coefficient $\sigma\ge0$, advective field $ eta$, force $f$, and trial pair $(u_h,p_h)\in V_h	imes Q_h$, define the strong momentum residual
$$R_{M,K}(u_h,p_h):=\sigma u_h+ eta\cdot
abla u_h-
u\Delta_Ku_h+
abla p_h-f.$$
For test pairs $(v_h,q_h)$, the full residual PSPG mixed form is
$$B_h((u_h,p_h),(v_h,q_h)):=
u(
abla u_h,
abla v_h)_\Omega+( eta\cdot
abla u_h+\sigma u_h,v_h)_\Omega-(p_h,
abla\cdot v_h)_\Omega+(q_h,
abla\cdot u_h)_\Omega+\sum_K	au_K(
abla q_h,\sigma u_h+ eta\cdot
abla u_h-
u\Delta_Ku_h+
abla p_h)_K,$$
with load $(f,v_h)_\Omega+\sum_K	au_K(
abla q_h,f)_K$. The **grad-div** addend in velocity tests $v_h$ is $\gamma\sum_K(
abla\cdot u_h,
abla\cdot v_h)_K$ with $\gamma\ge0$. This definition alone asserts no inf-sup condition, pressure bound, energy estimate, or convergence result.

For piecewise affine velocities, $\Delta_Ku_h=0$ on each cell. Therefore the standard P1 PSPG residual omits the cellwise viscous Laplacian of the exact velocity; this fact does not justify a pressure-accuracy or convergence claim. Such conclusions require separate consistency and stabilization analysis.

items.title: Finite-dimensional resolved–unresolved VMS split and residual closure
items.statement:
Let $X_c$ and $X_f$ be finite-dimensional real vector spaces and set $X=X_c\oplus X_f$; elements are written $(u_c,u_f)$, with $u_c$ the resolved component and $u_f$ the unresolved component. For a real vector space $Y$, let $Y^*$ be its space of real linear functionals. Let $A_{cc}:X_c\to X_c^*$, $A_{cf}:X_f\to X_c^*$, $A_{fc}:X_c\to X_f^*$, and $A_{ff}:X_f\to X_f^*$ be linear maps, with $A_{ff}$ invertible, and let $F_c\in X_c^*$ and $F_f\in X_f^*$. The linear equation on $X$ has block form
$$\begin{pmatrix}A_{cc}&A_{cf}\\A_{fc}&A_{ff}\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}u_c\\u_f\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}F_c\\F_f\end{pmatrix}.$$
The fine residual for a resolved vector $v_c$ is $r_f(v_c):=F_f-A_{fc}v_c$. Exact elimination gives $u_f=A_{ff}^{-1}r_f(u_c)$ and the Schur equation
$$\left(A_{cc}-A_{cf}A_{ff}^{-1}A_{fc}\right)u_c=F_c-A_{cf}A_{ff}^{-1}F_f.$$

A **residual closure** selects a linear map $T:X_f^*\to X_f$ to approximate the exact inverse $A_{ff}^{-1}:X_f^*\to X_f$. It defines $\widetilde A_{cc}:=A_{cc}-A_{cf}TA_{fc}$, $\widetilde F_c:=F_c-A_{cf}TF_f$, and the modeled fine component $\widetilde u_f:=T r_f(\widetilde u_c)$, where $\widetilde u_c$ solves $\widetilde A_{cc}\widetilde u_c=\widetilde F_c$. This is a finite-dimensional algebraic closure; an application to a PDE requires its own residual, spaces, invertibility, and approximation-defect analysis.

items.title: One-dimensional residual SUPG form with the exact cell parameter
items.statement:
Use the uniform mesh, coefficients, and spaces of [[def-supg-one-dimensional-convection-diffusion-model]]. On every cell set
$$\tau=\frac{h}{2|b|}\left(\coth(\mathrm{Pe})-\frac1{\mathrm{Pe}}\right),\qquad \coth s:=\frac{\cosh s}{\sinh s}.$$
For $w\in S_h(g_0,g_1)+C^2([0,1])$ and $v_h\in V_h$, define
$$a_h(w,v_h):=\epsilon\int_0^1w'v_h'\,dx+b\int_0^1w'v_h\,dx+\sum_{K\in\mathcal T_h}\tau\int_K(-\epsilon w''+bw')(bv_h')\,dx,$$
$$F_h(v_h):=\int_0^1fv_h\,dx+\sum_{K\in\mathcal T_h}\tau\int_K f(bv_h')\,dx.$$
Second derivatives are taken classically on each cell. The strong equation residual is $R_K(w):=-\epsilon w''+bw'-f$. For P1 trial functions, $w_h''=0$ on each cell, so the cell term is $\tau\int_K(bw_h')(bv_h')$. On the smooth consistency extension it retains $-\epsilon w''$; thus the full residual pairing is $\tau\int_K(R_K(w)+f)(bv_h')$, while the load contains the matching $f$ term. The SUPG equation is $a_h(w_h,v_h)=F_h(v_h)$ and adds the same residual-weighted streamline test perturbation to the differential equation and its load.

items.title: Multidimensional P1 SUPG residual form and parameter scaling
items.statement:
Use the model and notation of [[def-supg-general-convection-diffusion-reaction-model]]. Define $s_b(K)=h_K/\|b\|_{L^\infty(K)}$ when that norm is positive and $s_b(K)=+\infty$ otherwise; define $s_c(K)=\omega/\|c\|_{L^\infty(K)}^2$ when that norm is positive and $s_c(K)=+\infty$ otherwise. For each cell set
$$\delta_K:=\theta\min\left\{\frac{h_K^2}{\epsilon},s_b(K),s_c(K)\right\},\quad 0<\theta\le\frac14.$$
The minimum is finite and positive because its first entry is finite and positive. This scaling gives $\delta_K\|c\|_{L^\infty(K)}^2\le\omega/4$.

For a trial function $w$ that is the sum of a cellwise smooth function and a member of $V_h$, and $v_h\in V_h$, define the element residual $R_K(w):=-\epsilon\Delta_K w+b\cdot\nabla w+cw$, and
$$a_h(w,v_h):=\epsilon(\nabla w,\nabla v_h)_\Omega+(b\cdot\nabla w+cw,v_h)_\Omega+\sum_{K\in\mathcal T_h}\delta_K(R_K(w),b\cdot\nabla v_h)_K,$$
$$F_h(v_h):=(f,v_h)_\Omega+\sum_{K\in\mathcal T_h}\delta_K(f,b\cdot\nabla v_h)_K.$$
Here $(g_1,g_2)_D:=\int_Dg_1g_2\,dx$ and $\Delta_K$ is the classical Laplacian restricted to the interior of $K$. For $w_h\in V_h$, $\Delta_Kw_h=0$ because $w_h$ is affine on $K$. No stability claim is part of this definition.

items.title: One-dimensional P1 interpolation has an L2 error bound
items.statement:
Let $0=x_0<\cdots<x_N=1$ be a finite interval partition with maximum cell length $h$, and let $u\in C^2([0,1])$. Let $I_hu$ be the continuous piecewise-linear interpolant with the same nodal values as $u$. Then
$$\|u-I_hu\|_{L^2(0,1)}\le h^2\|u''\|_{L^\infty(0,1)}.$$

items.title: Shape-regular affine P1 interpolation estimates for C2 functions
items.statement:
Use the fixed dimension $d\ge2$ and the finite shape-regular affine simplicial mesh family from [[def-supg-general-convection-diffusion-reaction-model]] and [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. Let $u\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$, and on each simplex $K$ let $I_Ku=\sum_{i=0}^d u(a_i)\lambda_i$ be its nodal affine interpolant, where $a_i$ are the vertices and $\lambda_i$ the barycentric coordinates. Set $I_hu|_K=I_Ku$ and $M_2:=|\Omega|^{1/2}\|D^2u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}$, using the Euclidean matrix norm for $D^2u$. There is a constant $C_I$ depending only on $d$ and the shape-regularity bound such that
$$\|u-I_hu\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C_Ih^2M_2,\qquad \|\nabla(u-I_hu)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C_IhM_2.$$
If $u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$, then $I_hu=0$ on every boundary facet.

items.title: P1 PSPG Stokes form is coercive in its stabilization norm
items.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded connected polyhedral open set, and let a finite conforming nondegenerate simplicial mesh have connected cell adjacency. Let $V_h$ be continuous vector-valued P1 functions vanishing on the boundary, and let $Q_h$ be continuous scalar P1 functions with zero mean. Let $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$, $
u>0$, $	au_K>0$, and $\gamma\ge0$. For the stationary Stokes specialization of [[def-supg-pspg-grad-div-stokes-forms]], define
$$B_h((u_h,p_h),(v_h,q_h)):=
u(
abla u_h,
abla v_h)_\Omega-(p_h,
abla\cdot v_h)_\Omega+(q_h,
abla\cdot u_h)_\Omega+\gamma(
abla\cdot u_h,
abla\cdot v_h)_\Omega+\sum_K	au_K(
abla q_h,-
u\Delta_Ku_h+
abla p_h)_K.$$
For the residual load, set $F_h(v_h,q_h):=(f,v_h)_\Omega+\sum_K	au_K(
abla q_h,f)_K$. Define
$$\|(v_h,q_h)\|_{h}^2:=
u\|
abla v_h\|_2^2+\gamma\|
abla\cdot v_h\|_2^2+\sum_K	au_K\|
abla q_h\|_{0,K}^2.$$
Then this is a norm, $B_h(z_h,z_h)=\|z_h\|_h^2$, and the discrete problem $B_h(z_h,\cdot)=F_h(\cdot)$ has a unique solution satisfying $\|z_h\|_h\le\|F_h\|_{h,*}$, where $\|F_h\|_{h,*}:=\sup_{y_h
e0}|F_h(y_h)|/\|y_h\|_h$. The estimate controls pressure in the mesh-dependent gradient stabilization norm; it does not assert a mesh-uniform $L^2$ pressure bound or convergence.

items.title: Finite-dimensional VMS residual closure has an explicit Schur defect bound
items.statement:
Use the block operators and residual closure of [[def-supg-variational-multiscale-block-closure]]. Equip $X_c,X_f$ and their duals with norms, and use the corresponding induced operator norms. Let $G:=A_{ff}^{-1}$, assume the exact Schur system has a solution $u_c$, and put $r_f:=F_f-A_{fc}u_c$. Suppose the closure map $T$ has $\widetilde S:=A_{cc}-A_{cf}TA_{fc}$ invertible, and let $\widetilde u_c$ solve the approximate Schur system. Then
$$\|\widetilde u_c-u_c\|\le\|\widetilde S^{-1}\|\,\|A_{cf}\|\,\|T-G\|\,\|r_f\|,$$
and for the modeled fine component $\widetilde u_f=T(F_f-A_{fc}\widetilde u_c)$,
$$\|\widetilde u_f-u_f\|\le\|T-G\|\,\|r_f\|+\|T\|\,\|A_{fc}\|\,\|\widetilde u_c-u_c\|.$$
The exact fine scale is $u_f=G r_f$. These bounds concern finite-dimensional algebraic blocks; they do not certify a universal PDE subgrid model.

items.title: The one-dimensional SUPG parameter is positive and bounded
items.statement:
Let $s>0$ and define $m(s):=\coth s-1/s$ and $c_*:=\min\{(3\sinh 1)^{-1},\coth 1-1\}>0$. Then
$$c_*\min\{s,1\}\le m(s)<1,\qquad m(s)\le s/2.$$
Consequently, for the parameter in [[def-supg-one-dimensional-residual-form]],
$$0<\frac{c_*}{2}\min\left\{\frac{h^2}{2\epsilon},\frac{h}{|b|}\right\}\le\tau<\frac{h}{2|b|},\qquad \tau\le\frac{h^2}{8\epsilon}.$$

items.title: Multidimensional P1 SUPG consistency, coercivity, and error bound
items.statement:
Use the model of [[def-supg-general-convection-diffusion-reaction-model]] and form/parameter of [[def-supg-general-residual-form]]. Assume Countable Choice, and let $u\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$ solve the stated strong problem. For every continuous, zero-boundary function $w$ whose restriction to each cell has square-integrable values and square-integrable weak first derivatives, define
$$\|w\|_{\mathrm{SD},h}^2:=\epsilon\|\nabla w\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2+\omega\|w\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2+\sum_K\delta_K\|b\cdot\nabla w\|_{L^2(K)}^2.$$
$$M_2:=|\Omega|^{1/2}\|D^2u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},\quad B:=\|b\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},\quad C:=\|c\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},\quad \delta_*:=\max_K\delta_K.$$
Then the discrete form is coercive:
$$a_h(v_h,v_h)\ge\frac34\|v_h\|_{\mathrm{SD},h}^2\qquad(v_h\in V_h),$$
the discrete problem has a unique solution $u_h$, and the method is consistent, $a_h(u,v_h)=F_h(v_h)$. Moreover, with $C_*$ depending only on dimension, shape regularity, and the interpolation constant,
$$\|u-u_h\|_{\mathrm{SD},h}\le C_*M_2\left[\left(\sqrt{\epsilon}+\frac{B}{\sqrt{\omega}}\right)h+\left(\sqrt{\omega}+\frac{C}{\sqrt{\omega}}\right)h^2+B\sqrt{\delta_*}\,h+\sqrt{\delta_*}\left(\sqrt d\,\epsilon+Bh+Ch^2\right)\right].$$
This is a P1 estimate for the stated strong regularity and parameter branch; it does not claim stability for unrestricted multidimensional parameters or weaker regularity.

items.title: One-dimensional P1 SUPG is consistent and coercive
items.statement:
Assume the one-dimensional model of [[def-supg-one-dimensional-convection-diffusion-model]] with homogeneous data $g_0=g_1=0$, and the form of [[def-supg-one-dimensional-residual-form]]. Let $u\in C^2([0,1])$ solve $-\epsilon u''+bu'=f$ with $u(0)=u(1)=0$. Then $a_h(u,v_h)=F_h(v_h)$ for every $v_h\in V_h$. For every $v_h\in V_h$,
$$a_h(v_h,v_h)=\epsilon\|v_h'\|_{L^2(0,1)}^2+\tau b^2\sum_{K\in\mathcal T_h}\|v_h'\|_{L^2(K)}^2.$$
The right-hand side is a squared norm on $V_h$. Consequently the finite-dimensional SUPG system has a unique solution.

items.title: One-dimensional SUPG energy error bound with explicit tau dependence
items.statement:
Assume the homogeneous one-dimensional problem and uniform P1 SUPG form of [[def-supg-one-dimensional-convection-diffusion-model]] and [[def-supg-one-dimensional-residual-form]]. Assume Countable Choice, and let $u\in C^2([0,1])$ be the exact solution and $u_h\in V_h$ the unique discrete solution from [[thm-supg-one-dimensional-consistency-coercivity]]. For every continuous, piecewise-H1 function $w$ with $w(0)=w(1)=0$, define
$$\|w\|_{\mathrm{SD}}^2:=\epsilon\|w'\|_{L^2(0,1)}^2+\tau b^2\|w'\|_{L^2(0,1)}^2,\qquad M:=\|u''\|_{L^\infty(0,1)}.$$
This is the product $L^2$ norm of $(\sqrt{\epsilon}w',\sqrt{\tau}|b|w')$, so it has the triangle inequality.
Then
$$\|u-u_h\|_{\mathrm{SD}}\le \left[h\sqrt{\epsilon+\tau b^2}+h\sqrt{\epsilon}+h|b|\sqrt{\tau}+\epsilon\sqrt{\tau}+\frac{h^2}{\sqrt{\tau}}\right]M.$$
With $c_*$ from [[lem-supg-one-dimensional-optimal-parameter]], there is a universal $C_*>0$ such that also
$$\|u-u_h\|_{\mathrm{SD}}\le C_*\left(h\sqrt{\epsilon}+h^{3/2}\sqrt{|b|}\right)M.$$

title: SUPG, residual stabilization and variational multiscale methods — Examples

items.title: A periodic Q1/Q1 checkerboard pressure mode is invisible to divergence
items.statement: Take the periodic square with a $2\times2$ unit-square Q1 mesh. At the grid node $(i,j)$, for $i,j\in\{0,1,2\}$, set $q_{ij}=(-1)^{i+j}$ and identify opposite boundaries periodically. Assume $\tau_K>0$ on every cell. These nodal values define a nonzero mean-zero Q1 pressure. It is invisible to the ordinary velocity-divergence coupling, although its PSPG pressure-gradient term is strictly positive.

items.title: A two-scale VMS closure attains its Schur defect bound
items.statement: Let each resolved and unresolved space be $\mathbb R$ with the absolute-value norm (and give its dual the corresponding dual norm). items.title: Overlarge streamline stabilization suppresses a one-cell solution
items.statement: Use $\epsilon=b=1$, $f=1$, homogeneous endpoint values, and one interior P1 degree of freedom on the two-cell mesh $h=1/2$. Replace the exact parameter $\tau$ by the deliberately oversized value $\widetilde\tau=M\tau$, $M>0$. The discrete midpoint value tends to zero as $M\to\infty$, while the exact midpoint value is fixed and positive.

items.title: A two-cell SUPG mesh misses the interior shape of an outflow layer
items.statement: Take $b>0$, $\epsilon>0$, $f=0$, and endpoint data $u(0)=0$, $u(1)=1$. On the two-cell mesh $h=1/2$, the exact-parameter P1 SUPG solution has the exact nodal value at $x=1/2$. Nevertheless, at a fixed point inside the outflow cell its error tends to $0.98$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$. The example separates nodal fitting from resolution of the layer inside an element.
